metadata.title: The effectiveness of mentoring, coaching, and induction practices for early career teachers: A scoping review

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This paper is a scoping review and does not analyze student-level microdata from TALIS or any other large-scale assessment. As a result, there is no sampling frame, complex survey design, or weight variable (e.g., student sampling weights or replicate weights) to apply. The review instead synthesizes findings across 78 included studies using a registered scoping-review protocol (IDESR000154). Therefore, PV handling and survey-weighted estimation are not part of the empirical pipeline in this article.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible Values (PVs) are generated for cognitive achievement scales in large-scale assessments, but this article is a scoping review that synthesizes outcomes across prior studies rather than estimating achievement scores from ILSA microdata. Because there is no student-level dataset used for PV-based scoring, PV handling is not applicable. Similarly, the paper does not report an imputation or missing-data strategy because it does not perform original quantitative modeling on a microdata file; it conducts literature screening, charting, and thematic synthesis.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: This is a scoping review (not an empirical ILSA analysis). The review included studies published since 2008, focusing on Early Career Teachers (ECTs) with formal qualification and less than five years of teaching experience in mainstream/ generalist roles (excluding teacher candidates/trainees, employment-based training pathways, special education teachers, and teachers in religious schools). Interventions had to be formal induction/mentoring/coaching programmes at any level (federal/state/district/school), excluding informal arrangements. Outcomes had to specify effectiveness-related measures (e.g., teacher effectiveness/practice, classroom management, identity/belonging/socialisation, retention); purely descriptive experiences without an identified outcome were excluded. The search was conducted in ERIC, Scopus, the Australian Education Index, and the British Education Index, with de-duplication and screening in Rayyan, full-text retrieval for included abstracts, and citation chaining; 10,649 results were found, 7959 screened at title/abstract, 476 full texts reviewed, and 78 studies included after exclusions and citation chaining.

main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TALIS the study leveraged the reported predictors to predict Literature synthesis outcome (not student-level prediction), finding that This article is a scoping review of mentoring, coaching, and induction practices for early career teachers (ECTs), not an empirical machine-learning study using TALIS or other ILSA microdata. The review synthesizes 78 included studies identified through a registered protocol (IDESR000154) and organizes evidence into four outcome themes: teacher development of self, retention, teaching practice, and student achievement. Across the included studies, the review finds substantial inconsistency in how “induction,” “mentoring,” and “coaching” are defined and operationalized, which limits comparability of effectiveness results. The review also reports that correlational conclusions are the strongest form of evidence most frequently available, and that study designs vary widely (observational, experiments, quasi-experiments, secondary analyses, and programme evaluations). Because no predictive modeling, PV scoring, or survey-weighted estimation is performed, the findings are best interpreted as evidence about definitional and measurement coherence rather than as quantified causal effects. data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is sparse with respect to ILSA program/cycle, PV handling, missing-data handling, weights, countries, and ML techniques because the article is explicitly a scoping review. It does not use TALIS microdata (or any other ILSA dataset) for student-level modeling, and it does not report performance metrics from predictive algorithms. Consequently, fields that would normally be populated for empirical ML papers (dataset_used, target_variable, top_predictors, and numeric model metrics) are not applicable to this review format.
